messages.author: edd4914c326b6d31
messages.subject: big multinomial: simpler not better
parts:
My collaborators were not wild about a model with a lot of interactions,
so I tried a much simpler one. The original interacted almost every
variable with respondent race and HIV status (3 levels of each). The
outcome had 5 levels. The only interactions in the new model were a few
interactions with race.

The simpler model behaves worse than the more complex one; in fact, it
behaves very badly.

I'm a little puzzled that this is happening. Though I thought the more
complex model would capture the data better, most of the coefficients it
estimated were quite small. Even if they weren't the behavior is
suprising to me.

I wonder if anyone has any comments about what these results might indicate.

DETAILS

The new model allowed the 2-way coefficients to have a different
variance than the lower order ones.
Summary of new model

n_eff Rhat

Min. : 5.427 Min. :0.9994

1st Qu.: 44.788 1st Qu.:1.0077

Median : 187.642 Median :1.0245

Mean : 359.331 Mean :1.0447

3rd Qu.: 667.268 3rd Qu.:1.0631

Max. :1577.461 Max. :1.4956


The old model had several batches of parameters, each with its own variance (3-way, split into 2 groups, and everything else).


n_eff Rhat

Min. : 109.6 Min. :0.999

1st Qu.: 631.8 1st Qu.:1.001

Median : 880.8 Median :1.002

Mean : 899.0 Mean :1.003

3rd Qu.:1143.2 3rd Qu.:1.005

Max. :2229.2 Max. :1.042

Both had 2,000 iterations in 3 chains.

iCluster+age+Born_US+educ_sg+jail+orientation+HIVReport+

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] big multinomial: simpler not better
parts:
No idea why the simpler model would have worse
convergence.

If you add interactions, the parameters should get
smaller, because the interacted parameters pick up
some of the prediction. So it seems to me that
you'd want different prior scales to account for this.
I'm going to start a new thread with a new subject
to ask about this, because I don't know the answer.

- Bob

messages.author: 146bc26797d1c5e2
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] big multinomial: simpler not better
parts: I have seen worse convergence with a simpler model when the data clearly did not fit the model. That was with a multinomial likelihood. Adding a huge number of extra parameters to account for "overdispersion" actually made convergence faster.
